title: Bit ribbons: Even-key census
topics: Recursion, sorting, binary search and bits
summary: For each nonnegative reading, produce the number of 1 bits in its binary representation. The reading 0 contributes 0. Return how many values in the derived sequence are even, including 0 and negative even values.
descriptionMd:
A punch ribbon stores its active holes as the set bits of a nonnegative reading. Sol separates readings for the office's even-numbered keys. A zero reading belongs in that count, just like any other even number.

For each nonnegative reading, produce the number of 1 bits in its binary representation. The reading 0 contributes 0.

Return how many values in the derived sequence are even, including 0 and negative even values.

Implement bitRibbonsEvenKeyCensus(readings, k). k is part of the common inspection-card signature and does not affect this task's result.
unitIntro: Bit counting. For each nonnegative reading, produce the number of 1 bits in its binary representation. The reading 0 contributes 0. Keep the sequence order specified here before computing the requested receipt. A scan invariant says what has been processed and what remains. Work through the proof strip first, then change the returned summary without changing the definition of that sequence. The last card revisits loop accumulators from Hello, Keys.
constraints: 1 <= k <= 8. All arithmetic results fit a signed 32-bit integer.

Target time O(n log M); auxiliary space including the derived sequence O(n). n is the input length; d distinct values; q query count; M maximum reading; V vertices; E edges; h tree height; r reported tree nodes.
hints: Start with bit counting. What state describes the portion you have already processed?

For each nonnegative reading, produce the number of 1 bits in its binary representation. The reading 0 contributes 0. Derive each required reading once; do not restart the whole procedure for every output position.
Return how many values in the derived sequence are even, including 0 and negative even values. Handle the empty derived sequence according to the stated return rule.

cases.explanation: The derived sequence is [3,2,3,0,2]. Return how many values in the derived sequence are even, including 0 and negative even values. This gives 3.
The derived sequence is [1,1,1,1]. Return how many values in the derived sequence are even, including 0 and negative even values. This gives 0.
The derived sequence is []. Return how many values in the derived sequence are even, including 0 and negative even values. This gives 0.
